claims.text: Increasing the fraction of a lightweight principal element lowers the density of a lightweight high-entropy alloy.
Increasing the lightweight-element fraction while holding the other principal-element ratios constant increases atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion.
Atomic-size mismatch among constituent elements induces lattice strain in high-entropy alloys.
Greater lattice distortion slows atomic diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion stabilizes a refined nanostructured phase.
Sluggish diffusion helps high-entropy-alloy microstructures remain stable at elevated temperature.
Stabilization of the nanostructure refines grain boundaries.
Lattice distortion enhances mechanical strength and resistance to deformation.
Lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion maintain alloy homogeneity under mechanical stress and elevated temperature.
The distortion–diffusion–nanostructure mechanism enables low density, high strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance to be achieved simultaneously.
An optimized increase in lightweight-element content will produce higher yield or compressive strength than the baseline alloy.
An optimized increase in lightweight-element content will lower corrosion current density relative to the baseline alloy.
An optimized increase in lightweight-element content will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the baseline alloy.
Above a critical lightweight-element concentration, excessive distortion destabilizes the phase balance.
Excessive lightweight-element content can cause segregation, amorphization, detrimental intermetallic formation, or transformation to a coarse-grained structure.
Phase destabilization above the critical concentration diminishes mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation performance relative to the baseline.
At sufficiently extreme temperatures, diffusion becomes fast enough to overcome the proposed benefit of sluggish diffusion.
The baseline alloy with moderate lightweight-element content has a stable nanostructured phase and balanced mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation properties.
